The sources are at 0; B, C, E, F, and H are one hop from a source; D, in the far corner, is the only node at distance 2. The table groups the nodes by distance." width="100%"} Runs one search that starts from all `sources=` at once and records, for every reachable node, the distance to the closest of them: hops on an unweighted graph, total edge weight (Dijkstra's algorithm) on a weighted graph. Sources are at distance `0`. Directed graphs are followed in edge direction. This answers "how far is everything from the nearest X" in a single pass, which is much cheaper than one search per source. Use `multi_source_shortest_path()` to also learn *which* source is nearest. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [sources]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[Union[int, str]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The starting nodes, as integer IDs or string labels. At least one is required. [cutoff]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Only include nodes at distance at most this value. If `None` (default), there is no limit. [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of the node attribute to store distances in. If `None` (default), uses `"multi_source_shortest_path_length"`. Nodes that are not reached get a null value. [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, returns a dictionary instead of self. If `False` (default), stores the distances as a node attribute and returns self for chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Union[dict[int, int | float], Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict=` is `True`: a dictionary mapping each reachable node ID to its distance from the nearest source. If `return_dict=` is `False` (default): returns self. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `sources=` is empty or contains an ID or label that does not exist, or a weighted graph has a negative edge weight. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} On a 4 x 4 grid with sources in two opposite corners, no node is more than three steps from a source: ::: {#b8e991e9 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec grid = ec.Graph().add_grid_2d(rows=4, cols=4) dist = grid.multi_source_shortest_path_length([1, 16], return_dict=True) max(dist.values()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 3 ``` ::: ::: Stored as a node attribute, the distances are ready for shading a plot: ::: {#b4a179bc .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} ( grid .multi_source_shortest_path_length([1, 16], attr_name="to_corner") .get_node_df() .select(["label", "to_corner"]) .head(5) ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
